Then, in Ancient Greece, the mathematician Archimedes came up with the clever idea to inscribe a series of polygons with increasing numbers of vertices on the inside of a circle (). For a polygon with n vertices, we obtain n triangles. The height of each triangle approaches the radius r as we partition the circle more finely. At the same time, its base approaches 2πr/n, since the ratio between arc and secant approaches 1 for a large number of vertices. Thus, the area of the polygon approaches n⋅r⋅12(2πr/n)=πr2.
